mainTopic: רבי יוחנן's מוחלפת השיטה tested against several משניות, then preparing young doves before יום טוב and the question of בְּרֵירָה
overview: The amud first tests whether רבי יוחנן was right that the names of בית שמאי and בית הלל are switched (מוחלפת השיטה) in the משנה about covering the blood (כיסוי הדם). The גמרא brings three cases where בית שמאי are strict and בית הלל are lenient: the pestle (עלי), the raw hide (עור), and the shop shutters (תריסין). Each one seems to clash with the blood משנה. The pestle and hide cases are each pushed aside by showing that the cases are different. With the shutters, בית שמאי can be explained, but בית הלל remain a problem. רבי יוחנן solves that problem by swapping the names, or else the shutters are special because there is no building or taking apart with כלים. Then a new משנה begins about preparing young doves before יום טוב. רב חנן בר אמי limits the dispute to the first brood. The גמרא then asks why בית הלל require naming specific doves, which leads to a discussion of בְּרֵירָה using a case of a corpse in a house with many doorways. רבא explains that the real worry is handling מוקצה birds, and the answer to the final challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the rejection of the dove contradiction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes showing that the doves case does not truly contradict the כיסוי הדם case. It then adds a second way to remove the contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: But where there is no embedded shovel, בית שמאי would not permit it. Or another answer: בית הלל only said their lenient rule here because the doves are only מוקצה, a rabbinic rule, so it is enough for him to stand and say 'I will take this one and that one.' But there, with digging earth, they would not be lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its rejection of the earlier proof for רבי יוחנן's switch. It shows two ways that the doves case and the covering-the-blood case can both stay as they are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First answer: בית שמאי are lenient about covering blood only when a דקר נעוץ was set up before יום טוב, so the earth is partly prepared. Second answer: בית הלל are lenient with the doves only because מוקצה is a rabbinic rule. Digging earth on יום טוב is a Torah-level מלאכה, so they stay strict there.

keyTerms.meaning: A shovel already stuck into loose earth before יום טוב
They only said their ruling up to this point (and no further)
An item set aside and not available for use on שבת or יום טוב

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא דָּקָר נָעוּץ — לָא.
phrases.english: But where there is no embedded shovel — no.
phrases.notes: The end of the first deflection, which began earlier.

phrases.english: Alternatively:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי בֵּית הִלֵּל הָכָא,
phrases.english: Beit Hillel only said their ruling here,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the doves case.

phrases.english: because it is a matter of muktze,
phrases.notes: מוקצה is only rabbinic.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעוֹמֵד וְאוֹמֵר זֶה וְזֶה אֲנִי נוֹטֵל סַגִּי.
phrases.english: so standing and saying 'this and that I will take' is enough.
But there — no.
phrases.notes: "There" means digging earth, which is a Torah-level prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the deflection of the dove contradiction that began on the previous amud.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the need to switch the opinions, based on the doves case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two cases are different: either the shovel was prepared before יום טוב, or the doves case is only a rabbinic prohibition while digging is Torah-level.

steps.title: Bringing the pestle case as a new source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the real difficulty comes from a different משנה, about using a pestle to cut meat on.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty: בית שמאי say one may not take a pestle to cut meat on it, and בית הלל permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new, stronger contradiction. It quotes a משנה about the pestle (עלי) that it will compare in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pestle is normally used for pounding grain, so using it on יום טוב raises a question of מוקצה. Here בית שמאי forbid using it to cut meat, and בית הלל allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: If there is a difficulty, this is the real difficulty
A large pestle used for pounding grain

phrases.english: Rather, if there is a difficulty — this is the difficulty:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: אֵין נוֹטְלִין אֶת הָעֱלִי,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: One may not take the pestle,
to cut meat on it,
and Beit Hillel permit it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the dove proof was rejected, a new source is brought in.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the pestle case, בית שמאי forbid and בית הלל permit.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of בית שמאי and בית הלל in הלכות יום טוב, compared with the כיסוי הדם משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the pestle case בית שמאי are strict and בית הלל lenient. This is the reverse of the blood case. The full comparison comes in the next step.

steps.title: The pestle contradicts the covering-the-blood case
steps.stepSummary: In the pestle case בית שמאי are strict and בית הלל are lenient. In the covering-the-blood case it is the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems that about שמחת יום טוב, בית שמאי are strict and בית הלל are lenient. But this contradicts the משנה of 'one who slaughters a wild animal or bird,' where בית שמאי are lenient!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the two משניות side by side and points out that each school seems to switch sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases are about getting ready for the יום טוב meal. In the pestle case בית שמאי are strict, but in the slaughtering case they allow digging earth to cover the blood, and בית הלל forbid it. That looks like an inconsistency in both schools.

keyTerms.meaning: The joy of יום טוב, especially the festive meal
And they set it against (another source) to raise a contradiction
One who slaughters a wild animal or a bird (which needs its blood covered)

phrases.english: Apparently, regarding rejoicing on the Festival,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי לְחוּמְרָא וּבֵית הִלֵּל לְקוּלָּא,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai are stringent and Beit Hillel are lenient,
and they raised a contradiction:

phrases.aramaic: הַשּׁוֹחֵט חַיָּה וָעוֹף, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וְכוּ׳!
phrases.english: One who slaughters an undomesticated animal or a fowl — Beit Shammai etc.!
phrases.notes: There, בית שמאי allow digging to cover the blood, and בית הלל forbid it unless the earth was prepared beforehand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the pestle source from step 2 to build the contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of בית שמאי and בית הלל in הלכות יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each school is strict in one case and lenient in a similar case, which shows an inconsistency.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the opinions are switched
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן solves the contradiction by saying the names in the covering-the-blood משנה should be swapped.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The opinions are switched.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that this pestle contradiction was the reason רבי יוחנן said מוחלפת השיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we swap the names in the slaughtering משנה, בית שמאי become strict and בית הלל become lenient there too. Then both schools are consistent.

keyTerms.meaning: The opinions are switched (the names should be swapped)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The opinions are reversed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Switching the names in a text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two schools seem to be inconsistent.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once the names in the כיסוי הדם משנה are swapped, each school is consistent.

steps.title: Rejecting the pestle proof as well
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the opinions are switched, and gives two ways the cases could be different.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Perhaps not! בית שמאי only said their ruling there where there is an embedded shovel, but where there is no embedded shovel they would not be lenient. Or another answer: בית הלל only said their ruling here because the pestle still has the status of a vessel, but there they would not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and shows that the pestle case does not force us to swap the names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First answer: בית שמאי are lenient about the blood only when the shovel was ready from before יום טוב. Second answer: בית הלל allow the pestle because it is a real כלי, so it is not fully מוקצה. Earth is not a כלי at all.
steps.confusionAlert: This step looks almost the same as step 1, but the second answer is new. Here the difference is that a pestle is a כלי, not that מוקצה is only rabbinic.

phrases.english: From where? Perhaps it is not so:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הָתָם
phrases.english: Beit Shammai only said their ruling there
phrases.notes: "There" means covering the blood.

phrases.english: where there is an embedded shovel,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא דָּקָר נָעוּץ — לָא,
phrases.english: but where there is no embedded shovel — no,
Alternatively:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי בֵּית הִלֵּל הָכָא
phrases.english: Beit Hillel only said their ruling here
phrases.notes: "Here" means the pestle.

phrases.english: because it has the status of a vessel,
but there — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether step 4's switch is really needed.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the pestle case as proof for מוחלפת השיטה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The cases are different: the shovel was prepared beforehand, or the pestle is a כלי while earth is not.

steps.title: Bringing the hide case as a third attempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries again, this time with a משנה about a raw hide placed where people will step on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty: בית שמאי say one may not place a hide before those who tread on it, and one may not lift it unless there is a כזית of meat on it. And בית הלל permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a third contradiction. It quotes the hide משנה, and the next step makes the comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Placing a raw hide where people walk on it helps tan it, so בית שמאי forbid it. They also treat the hide as מוקצה unless it has a כזית of meat on it, and בית הלל are lenient. This pattern will again be compared to the covering-the-blood case.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who tread or trample on it
The size of an olive (a halachic measure)

phrases.english: Rather, if there is a difficulty — this is the difficulty:
Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין נוֹתְנִין אֶת הָעוֹר לִפְנֵי הַדּוֹרְסָן,
phrases.english: One may not place the hide before those who tread on it,
phrases.notes: Treading on the hide is like tanning it.

phrases.english: and one may not lift it,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יֵשׁ עָלָיו כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר.
phrases.english: unless there is an olive-bulk of meat on it.
And Beit Hillel permit it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the pestle proof was rejected, a new source is brought in.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of the schools, compared again with the כיסוי הדם משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the hide case בית שמאי are strict and בית הלל lenient, which is the reverse of the blood case. The full comparison continues next.

steps.title: The hide case seems to contradict the covering-the-blood case
steps.stepSummary: From the hide case, בית שמאי are strict and בית הלל are lenient about שמחת יום טוב. That clashes with the covering-the-blood משנה, where it is the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: So for rejoicing on יום טוב, בית שמאי are strict and בית הלל are lenient. But this clashes with the משנה about someone who slaughters a wild animal or a bird on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge it started with the raw hide case. It points out that this looks like the opposite of the covering-the-blood משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the hide case, בית הלל let you put a hide where people will step on it, and בית שמאי forbid it. In the covering-the-blood case, בית שמאי allow digging up dirt, and בית הלל require dirt that was prepared beforehand. So each side seems to switch positions.

keyTerms.meaning: Rejoicing on the festival, especially with meat and food

phrases.english: So we see, regarding rejoicing on the festival,
Beit Shammai are strict
phrases.notes: They forbid placing the hide to be trampled.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel are lenient,

phrases.aramaic: וּרְמִינְהִי: הַשּׁוֹחֵט חַיָּה וְעוֹף בְּיוֹם טוֹב וְכוּ׳,
phrases.english: and contrast it: One who slaughters a wild animal or bird on a festival, etc.
phrases.notes: The covering-the-blood משנה, where בית שמאי are lenient and בית הלל are strict.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge from the hide case that step 6 opened.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of בית שמאי and בית הלל across the hide case and the covering-the-blood case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the hide case בית הלל are lenient, but in the blood case they are strict. בית שמאי show the reverse pattern.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן again says the names are swapped
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers the same way as before: in the covering-the-blood משנה, the opinions of בית שמאי and בית הלל should be reversed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The opinions are switched.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן fixes this contradiction exactly as he fixed the pestle contradiction, by swapping the names in the blood משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we swap the names, בית שמאי become strict in the blood case and בית הלל become lenient. That matches the hide case, so the contradiction disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: The opinions are switched (the names should be swapped)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The opinions are reversed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the blood משנה had the names in the right order.
steps.terutzMaskana: The names in the blood משנה are reversed, so both houses stay consistent.

steps.title: Again, the two cases might just be different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof for רבי יוחנן's swap. בית שמאי may be lenient only when there is a shovel already stuck in loose earth (דקר נעוץ). Or בית הלל may be lenient on the hide only because it is fit to lean on.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Maybe that is not so. בית שמאי only said their ruling there, where a shovel is already stuck in the ground, but not where there is none. Or: בית הלל only said their ruling here because the hide is fit to recline on, but not there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats its earlier pushback: the cases are not truly the same, so there is no real contradiction and no need to swap names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a דקר נעוץ, the dirt was already loosened before יום טוב, so digging it is easy and allowed, even for בית שמאי. The hide is usable as a seat, so it is not fully off-limits, and that explains why בית הלל are lenient there but not with plain dirt.

keyTerms.meaning: A shovel or spade already stuck in loose earth from before יום טוב
They only said this in a case where...
To recline or lean on it

phrases.english: From where? Perhaps it is not so:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הָתָם
phrases.english: Beit Shammai only said so there
phrases.notes: In the covering-the-blood case.

phrases.english: where there is a shovel stuck in the ground,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא דָּקָר נָעוּץ — לָא.
phrases.english: but where there is no stuck shovel, not.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי בֵּית הִלֵּל הָכָא,
phrases.english: Alternatively: Beit Hillel only said so here,
phrases.notes: In the hide case.

phrases.english: because it is fit to recline on,
but there, not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the need for רבי יוחנן's swap in step 8 by separating the cases.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the hide case as proof that the blood משנה must be swapped
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The cases differ: the blood case may involve a דקר נעוץ, and the hide is useful as a seat.

steps.title: The real difficulty comes from the shop shutters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a stronger source. בית שמאי forbid removing shop shutters on יום טוב, and בית הלל even allow putting them back. This again clashes with the blood משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty: בית שמאי say you may not remove the shutters on יום טוב, and בית הלל permit even putting them back. So for rejoicing on יום טוב, בית שמאי are strict and בית הלל are lenient. But this clashes with the משנה about someone who slaughters a wild animal or a bird on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: Because the hide case was not convincing, the גמרא switches to a new case, opening shop shutters on יום טוב, as a better source for the contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Opening the shutters lets people buy food for the holiday, so it is about שמחת יום טוב. Here בית הלל are very lenient and בית שמאי are strict, which is again the opposite of the blood משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: If there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty
Shutters or boards that close a shop

phrases.english: Rather, if there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty:
Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְסַלְּקִין אֶת הַתְּרִיסִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: One may not remove the shutters on a festival,
and Beit Hillel permit even putting them back.
So we see, regarding rejoicing on the festival,
Beit Shammai are strict
and Beit Hillel are lenient,

phrases.aramaic: וּרְמִינְהִי: הַשּׁוֹחֵט חַיָּה וְעוֹף בְּיוֹם טוֹב וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: and contrast it: One who slaughters a wild animal or bird on a festival, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected hide source with a stronger source, the shutters.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of בית שמאי and בית הלל between the shutters case and the blood case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the shutters case בית הלל are lenient for שמחת יום טוב, but in the blood case they are strict. בית שמאי show the reverse pattern.

steps.title: בית שמאי can be explained, but בית הלל remain a problem
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction within בית שמאי can be solved: the blood case has a דקר נעוץ and the shutters case does not. The contradiction within בית הלל stays difficult.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is fine that בית שמאי against בית שמאי is no problem: there, a shovel is stuck in the ground, and here, there is no stuck shovel. But בית הלל against בית הלל is a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sorts out which half of the contradiction is real. It explains away בית שמאי and confirms that בית הלל is the real problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The דקר נעוץ idea explains why בית שמאי can be lenient with the blood and strict with the shutters. Nothing like that explains why בית הלל are lenient with the shutters but strict with the dirt, so that difficulty remains.

keyTerms.meaning: But (introducing the part that is still a problem)
בית הלל against בית הלל (a contradiction within their own rulings)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the whole question is answered here. This step solves only the בית שמאי side. The בית הלל side is answered in steps 12 and 13.
steps.whatToRemember: With the shutters source, only בית הלל's inconsistency is still a real question. Steps 12 and 13 answer it.

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אַבֵּית שַׁמַּאי לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Granted, Beit Shammai against Beit Shammai is not difficult:
there, where there is a stuck shovel,
here, there is no stuck shovel.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בֵּית הִלֵּל אַבֵּית הִלֵּל קַשְׁיָא!
phrases.english: But Beit Hillel against Beit Hillel is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אַבֵּית שַׁמַּאי לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the contradiction from step 10 down to בית הלל only, using the דקר נעוץ idea from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of בית הלל between the shutters case and the blood case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No difference like דקר נעוץ explains why בית הלל are lenient with the shutters but strict about dirt for covering blood.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן swaps the opinions
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers the remaining contradiction about בית הלל by saying the opinions in the covering-the-blood משנה are reversed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The opinions are switched.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the open difficulty from Step 11 about בית הלל. רבי יוחנן says the names in the blood משנה are switched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the shutters case בית הלל are lenient, but in the blood משנה they look strict. If we switch the names in the blood משנה, בית הלל become lenient there too, and the clash is gone. This is the same move רבי יוחנן made in Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: the line of opinions (who holds what)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The opinions are reversed.
phrases.notes: Switch בית שמאי and בית הלל in the covering-the-blood משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty left open in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation: the names in one source are swapped
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources truly disagree about בית הלל's view on שמחת יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once the blood משנה is reversed, בית הלל are lenient in both places.

steps.title: Second answer: no building or taking apart with vessels
steps.stepSummary: Another answer that needs no swap: בית הלל are lenient about shutters only because shutters are כלים, and the rules of building and taking apart do not apply to vessels. In the slaughtering case, they would not be lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: בית הלל only said this here because there is no building with vessels and no taking apart with vessels. But there, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to solve the contradiction about בית הלל without changing the text. It says the shutters case is special.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking off or putting back shutters is not real בונה or סותר, because those labors do not apply to כלים. So בית הלל's leniency there says nothing about the blood case, which has no such reason to be lenient. The two sources describe different cases, so there is no real clash.

keyTerms.meaning: they only said it up to here (their view is limited to this case)
there is no building with vessels
there is no taking apart with vessels

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the clash about בית הלל: (1) רבי יוחנן swaps the opinions; (2) there is no swap, because the shutters are כלים, which have no building or taking apart.

phrases.english: Alternatively:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי בֵּית הִלֵּל הָכָא,
phrases.english: Beit Hillel only said their lenient view here (by the shutters)
because there is no building with vessels
and there is no taking apart with vessels.
But there (the blood case), they would not be lenient.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי בֵּית הִלֵּל הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same difficulty that Step 12 answered, without changing the text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית הלל's leniency about shutters shows they are lenient for שמחת יום טוב in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: The shutters leniency comes from a special reason, vessels, so it cannot be applied to the blood case.

steps.title: New משנה: preparing young doves before יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say a person may not take young doves on יום טוב unless he shook them the day before. בית הלל say it is enough to stand there and say which ones he will take.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: בית שמאי say he may not take unless he shook them while it was still day. בית הלל say he stands and says, "This one and that one I will take."
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It is about how to prepare young doves in a dovecote before יום טוב so they may be taken on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals that were not set aside before יום טוב are מוקצה. בית שמאי require a physical act of preparation, shaking the birds. בית הלל say that a spoken statement made before יום טוב is enough preparation.

keyTerms.meaning: while it was still day (before יום טוב began)
"This one and that one I will take"

steps.confusionAlert: In בית הלל's view, the person speaks before יום טוב, not on יום טוב itself. The statement is the preparation that makes the birds usable later.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: Beit Shammai say:
One may not take (the young doves) unless
he shook them while it was still day.
And Beit Hillel say:
He stands and says
"This one and that one I will take."

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: לֹא יִטּוֹל אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִעְנַע מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי require a physical shaking before יום טוב. בית הלל say a spoken statement before יום טוב is enough.

steps.title: The dispute is only about the first brood
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן בר אמי limits the argument to the first brood. בית שמאי decree that he must shake them, because he may change his mind. בית הלל make no such decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן בר אמי said: The dispute is about the first brood. בית שמאי hold we make a decree, since perhaps he will reconsider. בית הלל hold we do not make a decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly where the משנה's argument applies. It is only about the first brood of young doves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People usually leave the first brood in the nest, so the person might handle the birds on יום טוב and then change his mind. That would mean he moved מוקצה birds for nothing. בית שמאי make a decree to require shaking, which shows a firm decision. בית הלל are not worried about this, so saying it is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא who explains the משנה
the first brood (first pair of young doves of the year)
perhaps he will come to reconsider (change his mind)

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Chanan bar Ami said:
The dispute is about the first brood,
for Beit Shammai hold: we make a decree
since perhaps he will come to reconsider.
phrases.notes: He may decide to leave the birds, and then he has handled מוקצה for no reason.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel hold: we do not make a decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר אַמֵּי: מַחְלוֹקֶת בִּבְרִיכָה רִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the case and the reasons behind the משנה in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is only about the first brood. בית שמאי decree because of a fear that he will change his mind. בית הלל do not decree.

steps.title: Second brood: everyone agrees saying is enough
steps.stepSummary: For the second brood, both sides agree that standing and saying "this one and that one I will take" is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for the second brood, everyone agrees that standing and saying "This one and that one I will take" is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנן בר אמי finishes his statement. He says there is no argument at all about the second brood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People normally do take the second brood, so there is no fear that he will change his mind. Without that fear, there is no reason for בית שמאי's decree. Even בית שמאי agree that a spoken statement is enough.
steps.whatToRemember: The argument in the משנה is only about the first brood, where there is a fear he will change his mind. For the second brood, everyone agrees that a spoken statement before יום טוב is enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that בית שמאי's demand for shaking is a protective decree tied to one specific worry, not a general rule that speaking can never prepare an item.

phrases.english: But with the second brood,
everyone agrees
that standing and saying "This one and that one I will take"
is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב חנן בר אמי's statement by explaining the case where there is no argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For the second brood, both sides agree that a spoken statement before יום טוב is enough preparation.

steps.title: Why must בית הלל name specific doves?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges בית הלל: why require naming 'this one and that one' instead of a general 'from here I will take tomorrow'?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to בית הלל, why does he need to say "this one and that one I will take"? Let him just say "from here I will take tomorrow"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule from the last step. If saying words is enough for בית הלל, why can't a general statement about the whole nest work?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 16, standing and naming specific doves was enough to prepare them for יום טוב. The גמרא suggests something easier: designate the whole nest in general, and whichever doves he takes tomorrow will turn out to be the ones he meant. That only works if the choice can be clarified later, which is the idea of בְּרֵירָה.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does he need…? (questions whether a requirement is necessary)
from here (from this nest, in general)

phrases.english: And according to Beit Hillel —
phrases.notes: Refers back to the dove case in steps 14-16.

phrases.english: why does he need to say
"this one and that one I will take"?
phrases.notes: Naming specific doves.

phrases.english: Let him say: "From here I will take tomorrow"!
phrases.notes: A general designation; which doves gets clarified tomorrow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule just stated in step 16 about what בית הלל require.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's requirement to name specific doves ("this one and that one").
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a statement of intent is enough, a general statement should also work, because the exact doves would be clarified when he takes them. So naming specific doves seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Blocking the escape: a משנה about a corpse in a house with many doorways
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא expects the answer 'בית הלל reject בְּרֵירָה' and starts quoting a משנה from אהלות to show that they do accept it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that בית הלל do not hold of בְּרֵירָה, didn't we learn in a משנה: If a dead body is in a house that has many doorways, all of them are טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shuts down an easy answer before anyone gives it, then begins quoting a משנה about טומאת מת. It is setting up a proof that comes at the end of this משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could answer step 17 by saying בית הלל don't accept בְּרֵירָה, so a vague choice can't be clarified later. The גמרא says: wait, we have a משנה where בית הלל do accept it. The opening rule is that when a body is in a house, every doorway is טמא, because we don't know which one it will be carried out through.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible answer that the גמרא then rejects)
Retroactive clarification: a later choice reveals what was meant all along
But didn't we learn in a משנה? (introduces a source that contradicts)

steps.confusionAlert: The topic suddenly jumps from doves on יום טוב to טומאת מת. The two cases are linked only by one idea, בְּרֵירָה. Watch for that idea, not the details of טומאה.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא בֵּית הִלֵּל לֵית לְהוּ בְּרֵירָה,
phrases.english: And if you say Beit Hillel do not hold of retroactive clarification,
phrases.notes: The possible answer the גמרא is about to reject.

phrases.english: but didn't we learn in a Mishnah:
phrases.notes: משנה אהלות 7:3

phrases.english: A dead body is in a house
and it has many doorways —
all of them are impure.
phrases.notes: Because the body might be carried out through any of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא בֵּית הִלֵּל לֵית לְהוּ בְּרֵירָה וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge of step 17 by blocking the obvious answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible defense that בית הלל reject בְּרֵירָה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה is about to show בית הלל accepting בְּרֵירָה, so that defense can't stand.

steps.title: One open doorway, or a plan to use one, keeps the others טהור
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: if one doorway is opened, or one was chosen for taking out the body, only that one is טמא and the rest stay טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of them was opened, it is טמא and all the others are טהור. If he decided to take the body out through one of them, or through a window four by four טפחים, that decision protects all the other doorways.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps going and explains how to save the other doorways from טומאה. This is still background for the key argument in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once it is clear which exit the body will use, only that exit becomes טמא. Clarity can come from a physical fact, one door being opened. It can also come from a person's plan, just deciding which exit to use. A window counts only if it is four by four טפחים, big enough for a body to pass through.

keyTerms.meaning: he planned / decided in his mind
four by four טפחים (handbreadths), big enough for a body

phrases.english: If one of them was opened,
it is impure, and all the others are pure.
phrases.notes: Now we know the body will leave through it.

phrases.english: If he decided to take it out through one of them,
phrases.notes: A plan alone is enough.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ בְּחַלּוֹן שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה —
phrases.english: or through a window that is four by four handbreadths —
it protects all the doorways.
phrases.notes: The plan saves all the other doorways.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִפְתַּח אֶחָד מֵהֶן הוּא טָמֵא וְכוּלָּן טְהוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the משנה begun in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once one exit is fixed, by being opened or by a plan, only that exit is טמא and all the other doorways are saved.

steps.title: בית הלל: a plan made even after death works
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי require the plan to be made before death. בית הלל allow it even after death, which shows they accept בְּרֵירָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: this works only if he decided to take it out that way before the person died. בית הלל say: even after the person died.
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the punchline of the proof. בית הלל let a plan made after death decide the exit backward in time, so they must hold of בְּרֵירָה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the moment of death, the טומאה already spread to all doorways because no exit was chosen. If a later plan can still save the other doorways, it means the later choice reveals which exit was 'meant' all along. That is בְּרֵירָה. So the challenge of step 17 returns at full strength: why can't the dove owner just say "from here I will take tomorrow"?
steps.whatToRemember: Step 17 asked why בית הלל need specific doves to be named. The defense "they reject בְּרֵירָה" seems to fail, because in טומאת מת בית הלל accept a plan made after death. That is בְּרֵירָה. So the question about the doves seems to return, and steps 21 and 22 answer it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This מחלוקת in אהלות is a classic source showing that בית הלל accept בְּרֵירָה. The גמרא now has to explain why the dove case is different.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
only if he decided to take it out
before the person died,
phrases.notes: The choice must already be fixed at the time of death.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say:
even after the person died.
phrases.notes: A later choice works backward. This is בְּרֵירָה.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים וְהוּא שֶׁחִשֵּׁב לְהוֹצִיאוֹ עַד שֶׁלֹּא יָמוּת הַמֵּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quoted משנה and delivers the proof that step 18 set up.
steps.raayaObject: That בית הלל hold of בְּרֵירָה, which undercuts the defense against the question in step 17.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה אהלות 7:3: בית הלל allow a plan made after death to decide which doorway is טמא.

steps.title: The doorway case only works from now on, not retroactively
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רבי אושעיא explain that בית הלל make the other doorways טהור only from the moment of choosing onward. So the case does not prove that בית הלל accept retroactive choice.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it already said about this משנה: רבה said, the point is to make the doorways pure from now on. And רבי אושעיא said the same thing: to make the doorways pure from now on. From now on, yes; going backwards, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from step 20. The אהלות case does not show that בית הלל accept בְּרֵירָה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20 the proof assumed that choosing a doorway after death works backwards in time. רבה and רבי אושעיא say it only works going forward: anything that became טמא before the choice stays טמא. Since nothing is clarified backwards, this is not בְּרֵירָה, and the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it stated about it? This introduces an אמורא's explanation that undoes the proof.
From here onward, only going forward in time

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבה is saying the choice does nothing. It does make the doorways טהור, but only for טומאה that comes after the choice. It does not reach back to before it.

phrases.english: But wasn't it stated about it (this משנה):
Rabba said:
to purify the doorways from here onward.
phrases.notes: Only the future is affected.

phrases.english: And so too said Rabbi Oshaya:
to purify the doorways from here onward.
From here onward, yes;
phrases.notes: The גמרא draws the inference.

phrases.english: retroactively, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It rejects the proof in step 20 by reading the אהלות ruling as forward-only.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from אהלות that בית הלל accept בְּרֵירָה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the choice works backwards. רבה and רבי אושעיא say it only works going forward, so no בְּרֵירָה is involved.

steps.title: רבא: בית הלל do accept retroactive choice, but worry about handling the birds
steps.stepSummary: רבא says בית הלל really do hold that the doorway choice works backwards. With the birds, their reason for requiring specific naming is different: a person might pick up and put down birds he will not use, and so handle מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: really, it works retroactively. And here, this is the reason: perhaps he will pick one up and put it down, pick one up and put it down, and so he will be moving something that is not fit for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a different way to answer the question from step 17. He keeps the idea that בית הלל accept בְּרֵירָה and gives a practical reason for naming the birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the person only says 'I will take from here,' then on יום טוב he will sort through the nest looking for good birds. Every bird he picks up and then rejects was מוקצה, and he handled it for nothing. Saying 'this one and that one' ahead of time avoids that problem, so the rule has nothing to do with rejecting בְּרֵירָה.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really. This signals keeping an original assumption.
He moves it and puts it down
Something not fit for him to use, meaning מוּקְצֶה

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the same rule can come from two very different reasons. One is a principle about choosing, the other is a practical concern about מוקצה.

phrases.english: Rava said: actually, it works retroactively,
phrases.notes: About the doorway case.

phrases.english: and here (with the birds), this is the reason:
perhaps he will move (a bird) and put it down,
move (another) and put it down,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָא מְטַלְטֵל מִידֵּי דְּלָא חֲזֵי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: and he will end up moving something not fit for him (מוקצה).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It disagrees with רבה's reading and gives a different answer to the question in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reason (טעמא אחרינא): the rule rests on a concern about מוקצה, not on rejecting בְּרֵירָה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Requiring 'this one and that one' means בית הלל reject בְּרֵירָה.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית הלל accept retroactive choice. They require naming the birds only so the person will not handle birds he ends up rejecting.

steps.title: Challenge: saying 'this one and that one' still leaves room to handle others
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: we said simply standing and saying 'this one and that one I will take' is enough. But he did not touch them, so on יום טוב he might still change his mind and handle other birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you said that standing and saying 'this one and that one I will take' is enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's reason using the ruling from step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the worry is that he will sort through the birds, naming them out loud without touching them does not seem to remove that worry. He might still not like them on יום טוב and start picking up others. So why is naming them enough?

phrases.english: But didn't you say:
when one stands and says,
'This one and that one I will take,' it is enough!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It challenges רבא's reason in step 22 using the earlier agreed ruling from step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reason, the concern about handling מוקצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Naming birds without touching them does not stop him from later sorting through them. So if handling is the worry, naming should not be enough.

steps.title: Answer begins: naming works when it is done before יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The answer starts: saying 'this one and that one' works because it is done on ערב יום טוב. The full explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies only on the eve of יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering the challenge, and the amud ends partway through. It is setting up a contrast that is finished on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because he chose the specific birds before יום טוב, he knows he cannot switch on יום טוב. So he will commit to those birds and will not handle the others. The coming lines will explain the contrast with a general 'from here' choice, which leaves the actual picking for יום טוב itself.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply only to, this is limited to

phrases.english: This applies only (when designated) from the eve of the Festival,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It begins answering the challenge in step 23 by pointing out that the choice was made before יום טוב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Naming the birds still leaves the risk that he will sort through them on יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Naming done on ערב יום טוב is firm, so he will not handle other birds. The full answer continues on the next amud.
